utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-95-12-PT, the Prosecutor versus Ivica Rajic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. For the sake of the record, could I have the appearances please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Kenneth Scott for the Office of the Prosecutor. I'm joined today by our case manager, Ms. Lakshmie Walpita and trial attorney Josee D'Aoust and Mr. Roeland Bos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I'm Zeljko Olujic, attorney-at-law from Zagreb, Croatia, representing Mr. Ivica Rajic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Rajic, can you hear the proceedings in a language that you could understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear, but I would like it turned up a bit. If we could only turn up the sound a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I hope somebody in the courtroom could help you to do that. And if you have any problems in the future to follow the proceedings, please let me know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's all right now. It's all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down, please. This is a Status Conference in accordance with the Rule 65 bis. The purpose of this conference are two. First, to organise the exchanges between the parties so as to ensure expeditious preparation for trial. Secondly, to review the status of the accused's case and to allow the accused to have the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto, including the mental and the physical conditions of the accused. Let's deal with them one by one. The first matter is about the preparation of the case. I would like to hear from both parties about the matter concerning the disclosure. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: May it please the Court. Your Honour, the Prosecutor's view is that disclosure in this case is being met. Our obligations are being satisfied, with the possible exception of three or four, perhaps, particular witness statements that we think need the Court's specific attention in terms of some protective measures as to those particular witnesses. We believe that our Rule 66 disclosure obligations have been fully satisfied. And as I reported to Mr. Harhoff yesterday, we did disclose, about ten days ago, some additional material. They were transcripts from prior ICTY cases concerning several of our witnesses. In looking at that further since yesterday, I can say that all of those witnesses had been previously disclosed and other statements had been disclosed. I'm just double-checking again, but yes, that's the case. So these were only additional materials. Other materials had been disclosed. The witnesses were known before. But these were additional transcripts that had to be further processed and translated into B/C/S before disclosed to counsel. As I say, with the exception of a very small number of items that we need to bring to the Court's attention, we believe that all Rule 66 disclosure has been provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. How about the translation issues? I believe that during the last Status Conference you mentioned that there are about 25 to 30 per cent of the documents which still needed to be translated from the B/C/S into English, or the other way around, and I would like to know, has the translation been completed by now or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I believe all the translations have been completed at this point. I will certainly double-check that, but it's my understanding that it's all been completed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could I hear Mr. Olujic on this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. It is true, if I may turn to the part where Mr. Scott said that something had been disclosed, a certain number of materials were disclosed ten days ago. I want to say that we actually received it three days before this Status Conference, on the 28th of August, more precisely. I would not like to have the practice repeated that materials be disclosed immediately before this Status Conference, because even with the best goodwill on my part, I have not been able to thoroughly review the material that was given me. Today, the Prosecutor has just said that all the material, with very few exceptions, has been disclosed. These few exceptions can include hundreds or even thousands of pages. I would therefore like to know precisely the number of pages involved. I would like to hear that from the Prosecutor so that we can prepare for our work. Your Honour understands that once I receive materials from the Prosecution, I have to double-check them with the state archives, or any other source they may be originating from, so that I can be ready for trial in terms of harmonising facts, a point that will be covered today, as I understood from Your Honour. I would like to hear precisely what amount of material pending we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: To my understanding, the material that has not been disclosed only concerning with some statements of the witness which the Prosecution would like to ask for some protective measures on those materials. But I'll give the floor to Mr. Scott for the clarification on that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, you're exactly right. Just very, very briefly in response to Mr. Olujic. I can assure the Chamber and I can assure Mr. Olujic, we have taken our disclosure obligations very seriously, and we believe that the vast majority of that material has been disclosed, much of it for quite some time now. I think the Chamber perhaps, and I hope, will understand and know from our prior dealings, my prior dealings with Your Honour and other Chambers, that I'm not going to overstate the case or say things that I don't think are completely true. I allow for the possibility, of course, in this volume of material, there's always the possibility that something will fall through the cracks and has to be corrected in the future. I always do allow for that. I allow for that possibility now, despite the diligence and abundant good faith on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor. I think we have met and are meeting all of our disclosure obligations. Having said that, Your Honour, you're exactly right. The only things that are have not been disclosed are approximately three witness statements. And it's only witness statement material. It's not documents, it has nothing to do with the archives. It is simply there are three particular items that require -- in our view, require the Chamber's additional attention before we can disclose them, and we will direct that to the Court's attention in the next days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, you did not answer the question put by Mr. Olujic. He asked specifically how many pages are those documents. Hundreds or thousands, or just give approximately, you know, pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: These are witness statements, Your Honour. As to a couple of the witness statements, I can't imagine that either one, and again to be very -- to possibly overestimate rather than underestimate, I can't imagine that either statement would be more than 20 pages. As to one set of materials, they currently consist of tape-recordings, so I can't give you a page length on that. One of the things that has to be done is they have to be transcribed. So unfortunately, Your Honour, that one I can't answer. But we're talking with a small amount. We're not talking about thousands of pages. We're talking about a small number of pages. Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. As for the protective measures, I hope you could file something in this aspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And how about the material of the Rule 68? Did you find any material in these areas?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We have again -- the Court knows that Rule 68 is a continuing obligation, and we have and continue and will continue to provide Rule 68 material on an ongoing basis to meet our obligations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any comments in this aspect, Mr. Olujic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The next issue is about the agreement on facts. I believe that it is the policy and the desire of the Trial Chamber to encourage the parties to meet together to discuss whether there's any facts that both parties are in agreement, especially for some material facts, which I mean is the background, the status of the accused, the positions, you know, so as to facilitate the proceedings. Maybe Mr. Scott could inform us about any development in this aspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, since the first appearance of this accused, there have been ongoing conversations and communications with Mr. Olujic in which the concept has been discussed in general about we ought to try to -- we ought to see what we can do about identifying things that are not disputed. To move that effort forward, on the 11th of August of this year, we sent a letter to Mr. Olujic enclosing a set of 200 proposed facts, numbered facts, for his consideration. We've asked him if he would be so kind to respond to us by the 30th of September as to any of those facts which he is prepared to agree, either in whole or in part and then hopefully, depending on his response, we'd be in a position then to move forward. So we're optimistic, or we're hopeful, anyway, that there could be substantial room for agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Olujic, would you please confirm that you received those list of facts and what's your analysis of those facts?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is correct that a letter was sent on the 11th of August to my law office, including that proposal, but it is also true that it is the tactics of the Defence, which we have never concealed, to do everything we can to agree or stipulate everything that is indisputable before the trial. I will, of course, review this proposal from the Prosecution, with the help of my client, of course, because we have to go through the entire material to identify indisputable matters, and I will shortly contact my learned friends from the OTP and try to stipulate certain facts, of course, taking care of the interests of my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much, indeed. I believe that I'm encouraged by the attitudes of both parties, and I hope this process will come to an end with some results by the 30th of September. And at that time, I would like to ask both parties to submit a written report on the developments in this aspect so that we know where we are and how we proceed during the trial in the future. Is that agreeable to the parties? Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Olujic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. The next issue is about the witness protection issues. Mr. Scott, at this stage, do you think you need some protective measures concerning the future witnesses in the trial?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Except for the items that we identified to you a few moments ago, so far, as far as we know, there has not been any problems that would require attention at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Olujic, do you have any comments in this aspect?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. We accept this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. The next issue is about the indictment. Here I would like to express the views of this Trial Chamber that we believe the indictment should be kept intact, which means that the less amendment, the better, under the condition that both parties share the same interpretation and understandings of certain phrase or paragraph. Mr. Scott, do you have anything to say towards this issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Only, Your Honour, that in the meeting with Mr. Harhoff yesterday, I understood that the matter seemed to be satisfied. I wouldn't have anything else to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Olujic, what's your views towards this issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regarding the indictment, we have already pronounced ourselves. At this stage, as we respect the decision of the Chamber, there is no need to elaborate on the issue any further or point out or elaborate certain things that would be addressed at trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. I would like to say that the Prosecution's clarifications of the indictment pursuant to the Chamber's order of 27th April, 2004 in response to the Defence motion on the form of the indictment had been received on the 11th May, 2004 and accepted by the Chamber. Well, let's come to the last issue, that is, the accused's health condition. Mr. Rajic, how about your health?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. At the moment, I'm feeling well, although I was shaken by an unfortunate event recently, but my lawyer will tell you more about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have any other matters to complain?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Olujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yesterday at the 65 ter conference, I shared with Mr. Harhoff a major problem that arose in connection with my client. The problem is that another indictee of this Tribunal physically abused and beat up my client. We informed the Registry of the matter. It is a person who is no longer a prisoner in the Detention Unit, that is, Mr. Tihomir Blaskic. My client was not only physically abused, but after the physical abuse, his capacity to prepare for his defence was reduced to zero. He took this very hard, and I must tell you that for about two months, or more than two months, we have been unable to communicate effectively and prepare for this case, which makes serious allegations against my client. The person concerned is no longer in the Detention Unit of the ICTY, and I hope the event will not repeat itself. But I do have to tell you, Your Honour, my client still suffers the consequences, and I don't think his physical or mental condition has been fully restored. We thought it necessary to inform you of this, Your Honour. Mr. Harhoff told me yesterday that he had given orders to the Registry to keep him posted, but we have no further information or follow-up from Mr. Harhoff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry to hear what happened in the Detention Unit, and I believe that this matter has brought to the attention of Mr. Registrar. And following the incident, he asked the commanding officer of the UNDU to carry out a thorough examination of the incident and file a report in this conclusion. He personally also wrote a letter to you, Mr. Olujic, telling you about the result of his investigation in this aspect. In his letter, he mentioned that on the same day of the incident the commanding officer issued a written warning to Mr. Blaskic, and warned him that another incident of this nature would result in the withdrawal of his privilege. Furthermore, in order to prevent reoccurrence of such an incident and for the safety of both detainees, Mr. Rajic has been placed in another part of the UNDU, where he will not be in the contact with Mr. Blaskic. I believe that you have received this letter, and if not, we'll make this letter available to you, Mr. Olujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I heard unofficially that a warning, a reprimand, was issued, and the warden, Mr. McFadden, penalised Mr. Blaskic in some way, but I haven't received that letter to date, so I hope that through your good offices, a copy of the letter could be forwarded to me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll make sure that you receive that letter, and I believe the Prosecution will have a copy of this letter. Well, at this stage, are there any other matters that the parties would like to raise? Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Not from the Prosecution, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Not for the Prosecution, Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Olujic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I believe this is all for this Status Conference. The hearing is adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
